findings.title: enableSqlExpressions has inverted, dead logic and ignores the feature flag
findings.body: enableSqlExpressions computes `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` (note the negation, so `enabled` is true when the flag is OFF) and then returns false on both branches. The function therefore always returns false regardless of the feature flag, and the variable naming is inverted relative to its meaning. If the intent is to hard-disable SQL expressions, the function should simply return false (or be removed in favor of an unconditional error) with a comment explaining why; if the intent was to respect the flag, the negation is a bug and the second `return false` makes the flag a no-op. As written, a future maintainer flipping the first branch to `return true` would re-enable the feature when the flag is *disabled*.

findings.title: No tests cover the disabled SQL expression path; existing parser tests likely break
findings.body: The PR replaces the DuckDB-backed implementation with stubs that always return "not implemented", so `sql.TablesList` and `NewSQLCommand` now always fail and `ReadQuery` returns an error for QueryTypeSQL. No test was added asserting that a SQL expression query is rejected via both entry points (`ExpressionQueryReader.ReadQuery` and `UnmarshalSQLCommand`/`NewSQLCommand`). Additionally, any existing tests in pkg/expr/sql (e.g. tests exercising `TablesList` against real SQL) will now fail since the function unconditionally errors; they should be updated or removed in this PR so CI reflects the intended disabled behavior and a regression (re-enabling execution) would be caught.

findings.title: TablesList retains dead DuckDB-specific SQL construction against a stub
findings.body: `TablesList` still builds a DuckDB-specific `SELECT json_serialize_sql('...')` command and passes it to `NewInMemoryDB().RunCommands`, which now unconditionally returns "not implemented". The quoting, command construction, JSON unmarshal and AST walking are all unreachable dead code, and the variable is still named `duckDB` even though the PR's stated goal is to remove DuckDB references. The error logged includes the full raw SQL (`logger.Error(... "sql", rawSQL, "cmd", cmd)`) on every attempt, which is noise for a feature that is intentionally disabled. Consider returning the "not implemented" error directly from TablesList and dropping the dead path.
